page_objective: Define how the SIPANEL brand system, engineering identity, design system, content ecosystem, component library, analytics infrastructure, and multilingual digital platform should scale over time without losing consistency, technical clarity, or industrial credibility.

expansion_philosophy.statement: SIPANEL should evolve as a controlled engineering-grade digital system, not as disconnected campaigns, temporary trends, or inconsistent visual experiments.

brand_system: Maintain one source of truth for identity, messaging, visuals, technical positioning, and usage rules.
Update guidelines only through structured review and approval.
Avoid trend-driven rebrands that weaken industrial trust.
Preserve SIPANEL's engineering-first positioning across all future channels.
design_system: Expand reusable components instead of creating one-off layouts.
Keep design tokens synchronized with frontend implementation.
Document all new patterns before production use.
Preserve responsive, accessibility, and RTL consistency across future modules.
content_system: Create SEO pages, resources, and case studies from approved content structures.
Preserve engineering-first tone across all future content.
Avoid unsupported claims or unverified metrics.
Expand educational technical content around façade, roofing, waterproofing, drainage, and industrial envelope systems.
frontend_system: Build scalable templates for landing pages, resources, case studies, RFQ flows, and technical tools.
Maintain performance, accessibility, multilingual support, and RTL behavior as the platform grows.
Reduce technical debt through reusable architecture and governance.
Keep analytics and tracking systems standardized.

rules: New components must follow existing design tokens.
New patterns must be documented before reuse.
Avoid duplicate components with overlapping functionality.
Every component must support responsive, accessibility, and RTL requirements.
Analytics events must be defined for interactive components.
Component behavior must remain predictable and scalable.
Every new content page must match a clear user intent.
Technical claims must be supported by proof or engineering logic.
SEO content must follow one-primary-keyword-per-page structure.
Case studies must include challenge, solution, result, and risk prevented.
Resources must solve real industrial or construction problems.
All future content must strengthen SIPANEL's technical authority.
forbidden_expansion_patterns: Generic blog publishing without technical value
Creating pages only for keyword volume
Using stock visuals instead of real proof
Marketing-heavy landing pages without engineering depth

rules: New pages must support localized routes.
RTL behavior must be tested for Persian and Arabic.
Technical terminology must be reviewed before translation.
SEO metadata must be localized.
Language expansion must not break layout or hierarchy.
Technical meaning must remain consistent across all languages.
Every new interactive component must include analytics events.
New conversion paths must be added to funnel tracking.
Resource downloads must be tracked by type and topic.
SEO pages must track CTA and technical engagement.
Performance impact must be monitored after new feature launches.
Naming conventions must remain standardized.
New features must not reduce Core Web Vitals performance.
Heavy technical tools must be lazy-loaded.
New image libraries must use responsive optimized assets.
Do not add third-party scripts without performance review.
Mobile performance must remain the priority.
Technical visuals must continue using progressive loading systems.

recommended_workflow: Map requirement to existing SIPANEL systems
Check whether an existing component or template can be reused
Define UX, engineering, content, analytics, and SEO requirements
Run design QA and technical QA before release
Measure performance and engagement after launch

monthly: Review resource downloads and lead quality

conversion_systems: Lead scoring based on technical engagement

risk_prevention_rules: Do not allow one-off visual styles into production.
Do not publish content without technical review.
Do not add untracked conversion flows.
Do not expand SEO pages without internal linking strategy.
Do not introduce components without accessibility and RTL testing.
Do not weaken engineering positioning through generic marketing design.
implementation_notes: Future expansion must strengthen the SIPANEL system instead of fragmenting it.
Every new page, component, resource, or campaign should map back to the approved brand system.
Scalability depends on governance, reusable components, verified proof, and measured improvement.
The SIPANEL platform should evolve through engineering discipline, not visual trend adoption.
Long-term success depends on maintaining technical credibility while expanding digital capabilities.
